title: Time's Embrace
note: The experiment that failed. Memory made this worse, 7 down to 5, because every lesson was about cross-shot consistency and the pipeline had no way to obey them. This is what drove the anchoring change.

brief.goal: A three-shot product film for a brushed-brass desk clock on a dark walnut surface.
brief.styleNote: Low warm key light from the left, deep shadow, cool neutral fill, shallow depth of field.

criteria.body: The brushed-brass clock is unmistakably the hero of every frame
The lighting, palette and surface stay identical across all three shots
The clock face reads as the same object in every shot

constraints.body: The primary subject in every frame is a brushed-brass desk clock.
A dark walnut surface is visible in every frame, serving as the base for the clock.
A low key light originates from the left side of the frame.
The key light creates a warm tone.
Deep shadows are prominently featured, contributing to the overall mood.
A cool neutral fill light is used to soften shadows without removing depth.
A shallow depth of field is consistently maintained across all shots, isolating the clock.
No on-screen text or logos are present.
No harsh specular blowout is visible on the brushed brass or any other surface.

lessons.body: Ensure the lighting setup, including key light position, intensity, and fill light temperature, remains identical across all three shots to maintain consistent shadows and surface tone.
Depict the clock face with the same design, color, and hand configuration in every shot to reinforce product identity.
Maintain a shallow depth of field, with the brushed-brass clock always in sharp focus as the hero of the frame.
Utilize a low, warm key light from the left, casting deep shadows, and balance with a cool, neutral fill light.
Maintain a consistent dark walnut surface texture and color across all shots, ensuring no variation in wood grain or smoothness.
Prohibit any on-screen text, brand names, or logos from appearing on the clock face or anywhere else within the frame.
Ensure the clock face maintains a consistent design, including numeral style (e.g., exclusively Roman or exclusively Arabic), color, and any decorative elements, identical in every shot.

Adhere strictly to the established lighting setup: low warm key light from the left, deep shadow, and cool neutral fill, avoiding any shifts towards bright, sunlit, or high-contrast black lighting conditions.
